title: Choose the redesign's visual world
question: The roll assigned Interchange. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Interchange
options.lineage: Metro wayfinding: Vignelli's subway map and station signage, Sofia Metro's line colours
options.thesis: Your portfolio as a wayfinding system, built for people with thirty seconds, like every good station sign.
options.viewport: A dark platform: a departures board lists the work (Plater, live, platform 1) beside a giant red line roundel and the Sofia clock; scrolling surfaces into the light, printed network map.
options.risk: A metro theme turns into costume if line colours become decoration instead of real wayfinding.

raised.raise: Numbered exits: press 1 to 3 on the board to open a project; the whole board runs from the keyboard.
Every project shows its working drawing beside the shipped screen, like a sign's fabrication drawing beside the lit face.
Case-study stations are numbered, linkable steps; the pinned scroll scene also works as discrete steps with reduced motion.
One light rule on the dark platform: only the selected row burns full white; everything else stays dimmed.

options.label: The Pass
options.lineage: A restaurant kitchen pass at dinner service: ticket rail, heat lamps, thermal order tickets
options.thesis: The portfolio runs like a kitchen at service: work arrives as tickets on the rail and leaves the pass finished.
options.viewport: A dark pass under heat lamps; a live ticket prints the headline and slides onto the rail beside the projects; tear one off to open it.
options.risk: The most literal reading: it ties your whole identity to restaurants and Plater, and themed portfolios are a common landing spot.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.lineage: Rail concourse departure boards at rush hour
options.thesis: The work as a departures board: every project a row, every change a cascade of flaps.
options.viewport: A full-width board: your name, discipline and three projects flip in letter by letter; selecting a row opens its case study.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and everyone reads a departures board; it holds audience identification but explains less about how you design than Interchange.
options.risk: One gimmick if every section flips; it needs strict restraint after the opening.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: The Windows Phone Metro design language
options.thesis: Chrome deleted: giant cropped lowercase type and live tiles are the whole interface.
options.viewport: Giant lowercase 'iliya dinev' cropped off the right edge; live tiles flip between Plater, Vault and Aura screens.
options.case: Bold and recognisable to designers; holds audience identification but loses product clarity because tiles show screens, not thinking.
options.risk: Designers may read it as a Windows Phone tribute rather than your own system.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The portfolio as a text-mode board you dial into at 2 a.m.
options.viewport: A title screen pours in line by line over numbered menu exits.
options.case: Hiring managers do not identify with bulletin boards, and text screens hide the work.
options.kept: Complete keyboard operation with numbered exits.

options.label: Desert Neon Sign Program
options.thesis: Each project as a sign: the dimensioned drawing beside the lit face.
options.viewport: A towering sign stack of projects with a chase-lamp arrow.
options.case: No link to product design in your audience's eyes; Americana would overpower the work.
options.kept: The working drawing shown beside the finished face.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One sheet folded through numbered steps into a finished crane.
options.viewport: A vermilion square folding step by step as you scroll.
options.case: Beautiful, but the metaphor says craft, not products that busy people use.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Attention as light: things glow as you approach them.
options.viewport: A dark field where projects bloom near the pointer.
options.case: Atmospheric but unrelated to your work, and hover-dependent.
options.risk: Fails on touch and reads as a demo.
options.kept: Only the focused element gets the brightest light.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark award-site portfolio played straight: cinematic hero, huge headline, bento grid of work.
canonCard.viewport: A centred huge headline over a dark atmospheric photo, square buttons, a bento grid of project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like your four references and most dark portfolios; it stands out only through execution.
